caption: 01 · INVENTORY — What is actually here?. Assign a persistent identifier to each object, file, recording, agreement, credential, and related record. Preserve original order and provenance before reorganizing for convenience.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what is actually here? within Who Owns the Archive?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · SEPARATE — Which interest attaches to which item?. Record physical title, copyright authorship and transfers, trademark or design records, contract limits, privacy, access, and conservation separately. One accession row may need several rights rows.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping which interest attaches to which item? within Who Owns the Archive?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · GOVERN — Who may possess, use, reproduce, lend, digitize, describe, and dispose?. Turn vague control into verbs, responsible parties, territory, term, approval, exceptions, recovery, and a source document. Unknown is a valid status; guessed ownership is not.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who may possess, use, reproduce, lend, digitize, describe, and dispose? within Who Owns the Archive?.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · STEWARD — What must remain usable after a transfer?. Require identifiers, checksums, condition notes, formats, contextual narration, rights evidence, audit history, and a correction route to travel with the archive.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what must remain usable after a transfer? within Who Owns the Archive?.
